title: CVE 2026 | The Complete Guide to New, Critical & Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities (Updated Weekly)
content_md: CVE 2026 covers every publicly disclosed software flaw assigned a CVE-2026-NNNNN identifier this year, and it is already the largest annual list on record. This guide is refreshed weekly. It explains how CVE IDs work, tracks the newest and most critical flaws, logs what CISA has confirmed as exploited, and shows how to decide what to fix first. What Is CVE 2026? How CVE IDs, NVD, CVSS and EPSS Work CVE 2026 is the set of security vulnerabilities that received a CVE identifier in 2026, each carrying a shared public name such as CVE-2026-31431 so that vendors, scanners and defenders all mean the same flaw. By 20 October, vulnerability data firm Craci had counted 81,927 CVE records published this year, against roughly 48,000 in all of 2025. Trackers count slightly differently, but all show 2026 far ahead. What a CVE ID means (CVE-2026-XXXXX format) A CVE ID has three parts: the prefix CVE, a year, and a sequence number. The year reflects when the ID was reserved, or the flaw became public, not when the bug was written.
